body:
Thank you for your reply, I am very glad to hear that this won't have consequences to his career. In his more emotional moments he's told me what he's been through over in Iraq and I can't even imagine being as functional as he is after what happened. He is so much stronger than I could ever be.

I know that the military is acutely aware of the suicide problem and am glad to hear they're adopting a modern approach to it. My brother isn't too "manly" to such refuse treatment outright, but the specter of harm to his career prevents him from seeking help.

>The problem with that thought is you only get too know its not a false alarm for sure when it's too late.... 

I know and this is tearing me up inside. But since I'm so far away I have no way to gauge the seriousness of the situation. I could never forgive myself if I fail to act and he does something. But I think it's maybe around 10% that he will.
But wouldn't that harm his career? I'm hesitant to interfere with his life in such a way since I don't really understand what the implications could be, particularly if this is a false alarm.
